Sample non-events for inference

Source: R/preprocess.R
sample_non_events.Rd

Given an observed event log, generate nested case-control data by sampling counterfactual sender–receiver pairs according to predefined strategies.

Usage

sample_non_events(
  event_log,
  n_controls = 1,
  scope = c("all", "appearance", "citation"),
  mode = c("one", "two"),
  risk = c("standard", "remove"),
  exclude_pairs = NULL,
  exclude_concurrent = NULL,
  allow_loops = FALSE,
  seed = NULL,
  max_attempts = 1000,
  shift = c("none", "exponential"),
  shift_scale = 1,
  window = NULL
)

Arguments

event_log

Data frame with columns sender, receiver, and time.

n_controls

Number of non-events (controls) to sample per realized event.

scope

Candidate set definition. "all" uses every actor observed in the data; "appearance" restricts to actors that have appeared in prior events (so the first event, with no prior events, gets no controls); "citation" matches citation networks where senders are restricted to the papers that debut at the current time and receivers must have appeared earlier.

mode

"one" (default) draws both sender and receiver from the same candidate pool (single-mode): every actor seen in either role can be a control sender or receiver, as in networks whose senders and receivers are one node set (e.g. bike stations, e-mail users). "two" samples sender and receiver from separate pools (two-mode): an actor seen only as a receiver is never a control sender, and vice versa, as in bipartite networks (e.g. species invading regions).

risk

Strategy governing the risk set. "standard" (default) keeps all unrealized dyads available across strata, whereas "remove" deletes a dyad from the candidate pool after it has occurred (useful for processes such as species invasions where a pair cannot reoccur). Under "remove", dyads firing at the focal event's own timestamp are also kept out of its control pool (concurrent events are not valid non-events at that instant).

exclude_pairs

Optional two-column data.frame/matrix of (sender, receiver) pairs that are structurally ineligible as controls and must never be sampled (e.g. an alien species' native range, or any dyad forbidden in advance). Columns named sender/receiver are used if present, otherwise the first two columns.

exclude_concurrent

Logical; keep dyads with an event at the focal event's own timestamp out of its control pool? Defaults to TRUE under risk = "remove" and FALSE under risk = "standard", where a tied event is still at risk at that instant (the Breslow convention).

allow_loops

Logical; can sampled non-events have identical sender and receiver?

seed

Optional seed for reproducibility.

max_attempts

Maximum resampling attempts per control before giving up (prevents infinite loops when candidate sets are small). With shift = "exponential" it is the number of rejection draws tried before the valid candidates are enumerated, so sampling never fails there.

shift

"none" (default) gives every control its event's time, so a global covariate (a function of time only, e.g. weather or time of day) takes the same value within each stratum and cancels from the partial likelihood. "exponential" samples controls from a time-shifted copy of the event process (Lembo, Juozaitienė, Vinciotti & Wit 2025, Section 4), so controls carry their own times and global effects stay estimable; see Time-shifted sampling.

shift_scale

Positive number \(\nu\): the shifts have mean \(\nu\) times the average event time, measured from the start of window (the paper uses \(\nu = 1\)). Larger shifts carry more information about global effects, but leave more events with no control. Used only with shift = "exponential".

window

Observation window c(start, end) for shift = "exponential". Defaults to c(min(time), max(time)); pass the true window (the paper's \([0, T]\)) when it is known.

Value

A data.frame containing the original events (event = 1) and the sampled controls (event = 0), grouped by stratum identifiers. With shift = "exponential" it carries attr(, "shift"): a list with the shift mean, the window, the per-dyad shifts (named "sender->receiver") and the uninformative strata that got no control.

Time-shifted sampling

With shift = "exponential", every dyad of the risk set (all sender \(\times\) receiver pairs for mode = "two", all ordered actor pairs for mode = "one") draws one shift \(h_{sr} \sim \mathrm{Exp}\), reused for every event on that dyad. Event \(k\) on dyad \((s, r)\) moves to \(t^e = t_k + h_{sr}\); its control is drawn uniformly from the other dyads whose back-shifted time \(t^* = t^e - h_{s^*r^*}\) lies in window, and is stored with time \(t^*\). The risk-set rules are evaluated at \(t^*\): exclude_pairs always applies; under risk = "remove" a dyad that has fired before \(t^*\) is not at risk; under scope = "appearance" both actors must have appeared in an event before \(t^*\). An event whose shifted risk set holds no other valid dyad carries no information and gets no controls. scope = "citation" is not supported, and exclude_concurrent is not used (control times are continuous).

Covariates for a control must then be evaluated at its own time: compute endogenous statistics with endogenous_features(cc, stats, history_log = event_log), which evaluates each row against the events strictly before it, and evaluate global covariates at each row's time. widen_case_control() then gives time_ev / time_nv and <cov>_ev / <cov>_nv, and a global effect is fitted with rem(~ nl(<cov>)), the baseline with rem(~ nl(time)).

References

Lembo M, Juozaitienė R, Vinciotti V, Wit EC (2025). Relational event models with global covariates: an application to bike sharing. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series C, 75, 583–600. doi:10.1093/jrsssc/qlaf058 .

Examples

data(classroom_events)
cc <- sample_non_events(classroom_events, n_controls = 1, seed = 1)
head(cc)
#>   stratum event sender receiver  time interaction_type weight
#> 1       1     1     14       12 0.125           social      1
#> 2       1     0     12       15 0.125             <NA>     NA
#> 3       2     1     12       14 0.250           social      1
#> 4       2     0      1       10 0.250             <NA>     NA
#> 5       3     1     18       12 0.375         sanction      1
#> 6       3     0     19        3 0.375             <NA>     NA
